causalModel.founding: A village grown where nine root-joined trunks stand in one ring; one tree by the Hist's reckoning, nine by the tribes' reckoning.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: The ring of trunks encloses firm ground and makes its own stockade, with one gap left unbuilt for a gate. The knoll stands 4.8 m above the water table on firm lowland, with poleable water 32 m west and the Archon-Gideon road 160 m south-west.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: A tribe that hosts the convocation's overflow and has grown rich on it, renting pitch-rights to delegations that cannot fit at the Tsoko camp.
causalModel.pressures: Hosting a province's delegations one month a year has made them arrogant the other eleven. Two neighbouring tribes now camp at Greenspring instead, on principle.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: A convocation held elsewhere would halve the village. The falling attendance the Root Talk ground counts publicly is already showing in their rents.

scaleGrounding.loreSource: world/sources/catalogue/type-recipes.json hist-village (3-8 villagers; one elevated member on the tree-minder's platform); world/sources/lore/extrapolation/settlement-register.md M3 band 12-35 with guests; UESP Lore:Hist, Lore:Argonian for the tree-minder, the naheesh and the uxith
scaleGrounding.why: Eight resident villagers in five households take the recipe's top band, because the village is rich on rent: the tree-minder and the watcher, the naheesh, the pitch-taker's household and two tribe families. The M3 band is reached only in the convocation month, when up to twelve guests fill the four rented huts and the two pitches. Fourteen structures: nine huts and a round house, the arch, the minder's deck, two shelters and a rack.

candidates.why: A firm-lowland knoll 149 m from the plot: 4.77 m above the water table, ground slope 2.6 deg and 2.17 m of relief across the whole 66 m ring, so eight of the nine trunks sit on a plinth or a pad and the elder trunk needs a dug-in flare. Poleable water 32 m west with the shoreline 40 m off, so the ring encloses firm ground rather than standing in it; the Archon-Gideon road passes 160 m south-west, which is the catalogue's road discovery; flood band 0 and no wet-season inundation.
The flattest ring in the neighbourhood, 1.66 m of relief. Closest to the road at 105 m.
candidates.rejectedBecause: The shoreline is 10 m from the centre, so the western third of a 33 m ring would stand in water. The record's site advantage is that the ring encloses firm ground. This candidate cannot deliver it.

candidates.why: The plotted position: firm lowland, 3.04 m above the water table, flood band 0.
candidates.rejectedBecause: 4.33 m of relief across the 66 m ring, which puts several trunks past the 2 m no-grading limit. The water is 66 m off and the road 241 m off. The macro plot could not see the local relief; the meso pass can.

districts.notes: The ring of nine trunks and the clearing it encloses: eight huts in eight gaps, the arch in the ninth, the naheesh's house and the minder's deck inside. One kit set; the trunks are landmarks, not buildings.

why.what: The ring: nine Hist trunks on a 21 m radius, eight mud huts in the gaps between them, the arch in the ninth gap and the clearing they enclose.
why.whyHere: The trunks grew here in one ring; the tribe built into the gaps because the ring is a stockade already made.
why.whyNeighbours: The pitch ground lies outside the gate on the road side and the landing on the water side, so both kinds of guest arrive at the one arch.
why.playerPurpose: The safe rest, the services and the lore of the place: every door, the nest, the hearing house and the fighting ground are inside the ring.
why.microGeography: The ring sits on a firm-lowland knoll with 1.5 m of fall from the north-western rise to the southern gap, 4 m above the water table and clear of the wet-season flood.

districts.notes: The rented pitch ground outside the gate on the road side: two shelters, a rack and the pitch line, on the same mud kit set. The canvas is the delegations' own.

why.what: The rented pitch ground: a fenced shelf south-west of the ring with two delegation shelters and a drying rack.
why.whyHere: The village's trade is renting ground to the convocation's overflow. The ground that it rents has to lie outside its own stockade.
why.whyNeighbours: It lies along the spur between the road and the gate, so every payer passes the pitch-taker at the arch while entering.
why.playerPurpose: The ground of Pitch-Rights and Under the Overflow, together with the empty pitches of Water Without Ceremony.
why.microGeography: A shelf at about 3 m, level within half a metre, which sheds south to the road and stays dry when the flats below it flood.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its long side follows the ring's tangent between two trunks and its door opens inward to the clearing, because the ring is the stockade and no door faces out.

why.what: The eastern family's hut, in the gap east of the elder trunk.
why.whyHere: The village holds two tribe families beside its three office-holders; this is the household charged with the nest.
why.whySpot: The gap east of the elder trunk is the nearest wall gap to the uxith, on the level northern floor of the ring.
why.whyNeighbours: It shares the elder trunk with the naheesh's house and the eastern guest hut with the rented arc.
why.playerPurpose: A family home a player may enter; the eastern household's talk is about the eggs and the guests.
why.microGeography: Ground at 3.8 m, a shallow pad; the hut's back wall takes the fall towards the eastern water.

parcels.orientationWhy: Set square across its gap on the eastern arc, door to the ring walk, so a guest steps from the walk into the hut and the rented arc reads as one row.

why.what: The first of three rented huts on the eastern arc, let to a delegation for the convocation month.
why.whyHere: The village grew rich on the convocation's overflow; a delegation that pays for a hut rather than a pitch is the top of its trade.
why.whySpot: The eastern arc faces the morning light and the eastern water, the side shown to a guest.
why.whyNeighbours: It is the first of three rented huts in a row, the row which a walker passes on the ring walk from the gate.
why.playerPurpose: A lodging for the player when the huts stand empty. It is the first door tried in Under the Overflow.
why.microGeography: Ground at 3.7 m on a pad; the arc here is the flattest run of the ring.

parcels.orientationWhy: Set square across its gap, door to the ring walk, as every hut of the rented arc is.

why.what: The second rented hut of the eastern arc.
why.whyHere: Two of the four delegations which once paid for huts now camp at Greenspring, so this hut stands empty eleven months and is let in the twelfth.
why.whySpot: The middle of the eastern arc, behind the root join at which the felling claim is argued.
why.whyNeighbours: It stands between the two other rented huts and backs onto the join of the felling dispute.
why.playerPurpose: The empty hut of Water Without Ceremony: the absent tribe's place, kept swept and unlet.
why.microGeography: Ground at 3.9 m on a pad; the join outside its back wall lies along the slope.

parcels.orientationWhy: Set square across its gap, door to the ring walk, closing the rented arc.

why.what: The third rented hut, the last of the eastern arc before the store.
why.whyHere: A third rented hut is the measure of the village's confidence; the rent ledger shows that it has not been let in two years.
why.whySpot: The south-eastern gap, where the knoll begins to fall to the flats.
why.whyNeighbours: It stands between the second rented hut and the store hut. The fighting ground of the clearing lies before its door.
why.playerPurpose: The second empty hut of Water Without Ceremony. It is the hut nearest the felling scene.
why.microGeography: Ground at 3.7 m, the hut set on a pad against the fall to the south.

parcels.orientationWhy: Set square across the southern gap, door inward, so the store is filled from the clearing and shows a blank wall to the road.

why.what: The store hut, where the village keeps the food and reagents which it holds for its guests.
why.whyHere: The type recipe gives every Hist village a food and reagent cache without a guard; here it is a hut, because the village has guests to feed.
why.whySpot: The southern gap, the lowest footing of the ring and the coolest hut, out of the morning and evening sun.
why.whyNeighbours: It sits between the rented arc and the road-side trunk, so a delegation's provisions travel eight paces from hut to store.
why.playerPurpose: The guest cache of the recipe: provisions a player may take. It is also the container socket of the rest-shelter reward.
why.microGeography: Ground at 3.5 m on a plinth, the lowest hut of the ring, its floor raised against the run-off from the clearing.

parcels.orientationWhy: Turned across its gap with the door to the clearing, so the pitch-taker sees the gate from the threshold without looking out of the ring.

why.what: The pitch-rights taker's hut, in the first gap west of the gate.
why.whyHere: The village's trade is rent; the household which takes it lives beside the gate through which every payer comes.
why.whySpot: The first gap on the water side of the gate, from whose door both the gate and the landing path are in view.
why.whyNeighbours: It shares the water-side trunk with the gate and stands over the chime frame its household dresses.
why.playerPurpose: The quest-giver's home for Pitch-Rights and the household paid to leave the baggage shut in Under the Overflow.
why.microGeography: Ground at 4.4 m on a pad, on the rise which begins the western high side of the ring.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its long side follows the ring's tangent between two trunks and its door opens inward to the clearing, because the ring is the stockade and no door faces out.

why.what: The western family's hut, in the gap between the western and north-western trunks.
why.whyHere: The second of the two tribe families; the household which works the landing and poles the boat to Uxaneet.
why.whySpot: The western gap, on the highest footing of the ring, nearest the landing path outside the wall.
why.whyNeighbours: It stands between the pitch-taker's hut and the tree-minder's hut on the quiet western arc.
why.playerPurpose: The boat household: the travel service to Uxaneet is asked for at this door.
why.microGeography: Ground at 5.0 m on a plinth, the high side of the ring, dry in every season.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its long side follows the ring's tangent between two trunks and its door opens inward to the clearing, because the ring is the stockade and no door faces out.

why.what: The tree-minder's hut, in the gap west of the elder trunk.
why.whyHere: Every Hist village keeps a tree-minder; the office lives against the tree which it keeps.
why.whySpot: The gap west of the elder trunk, so the minder's back wall stands against the elder trunk's root.
why.whyNeighbours: It shares the elder trunk with the naheesh's house. The minder's deck stands across the clearing from its door.
why.playerPurpose: The tree-minder's home in The Child of Two Hist, where the minder's testimony is given.
why.microGeography: Ground at 4.5 m on a pad, on the north-western rise.

parcels.orientationWhy: Turned to the gate so the naheesh's door looks down the path to the arch and an arriving delegation is seen the length of the clearing.

why.what: The naheesh's house, the round house at the foot of the elder trunk, where the Root Talk is carried and guests are received.
why.whyHere: The office-holder who carries the Root Talk to the convocation needs a house in which delegations can be heard; the village's standing rests on it.
why.whySpot: It stands inside the ring at the foot of the elder trunk, drawn back off the wall so that the trunk rises clear behind its roof.
why.whyNeighbours: The tree-minder's hut and the eastern family's hut flank it in the wall; the uxith stands to its east and the path from the gate ends at its door.
why.playerPurpose: The hearing house of The Child of Two Hist and the evidence socket of the identity case; the door to which every approach leads.
why.microGeography: It occupies the level 4.0 m floor at the north of the clearing, the highest and driest ground inside the ring.

parcels.orientationWhy: The deck faces the elder trunk across the clearing, because the watcher's post exists to watch that trunk.

why.what: The tree-minder's deck, a low woven platform from which the watcher keeps the elder trunk in view.
why.whyHere: The type recipe raises one member of every Hist village onto the tree-minder's platform; here that member is the watcher.
why.whySpot: It stands on the south-western floor of the clearing, off the path from the gate and outside the fighting ground to the east, with the elder trunk 31 m before it.
why.whyNeighbours: The pitch-taker's hut and the chime frame stand behind it and the naheesh's house before it.
why.playerPurpose: The tree-minder's station in The Child of Two Hist; the npc socket sits on it.
why.microGeography: A pad on the 4.1 m floor; the deck's 0.34 m rise is enough to see over the seated crowd of a convocation.

parcels.orientationWhy: The arch stands square across the heartland track where it reaches the ring, so a walker passes through the opening rather than round the posts.

why.what: The stick arch which stands across the ninth gap of the ring, the one gap left unbuilt.
why.whyHere: A ring with eight huts in nine gaps needs one gap for a door. A village which lives on guests marks its door.
why.whySpot: The south-western gap faces the spur and the landing path together, so one arch serves both approaches.
why.whyNeighbours: The pitch-taker's hut stands on its right hand and the road-side trunk on its left; the chime frame hangs inside it.
why.playerPurpose: The threshold of the village: the spur passes under it, the ring walk and the path to the naheesh's house begin inside it. The pitch ledger is kept beside it.
why.microGeography: It stands on the 4.1 m lip of the knoll where the spur's climb levels, so an arrival steps through it onto flat ground.

parcels.orientationWhy: The open side of the shelter faces east up the pitch path, so a delegation pitching here looks back down the spur of its arrival.

why.what: The first delegation shelter on the rented pitch ground, an open canvas struck and re-pitched by the month.
why.whyHere: Delegations that cannot fit at the Tsoko camp pitch here and pay for the ground; the canvas is theirs, the ground is the village's.
why.whySpot: The nearer pitch, where the pitch path from the spur ends, on the flat 3 m shelf south-west of the ring.
why.whyNeighbours: It stands inside the pitch line, with the second pitch behind it and the drying rack at the mouth of the ground.
why.playerPurpose: The delegation baggage of Under the Overflow is stacked under this canvas; the container socket sits in it.
why.microGeography: The shelf here is level within 0.5 m over the whole ground and sheds to the south, so the pitch stays dry.

parcels.orientationWhy: Turned a little across the fall of the shelf so its canvas sheds run-off away from the pitch path rather than across it.

why.what: The second delegation shelter, the further pitch of the ground.
why.whyHere: Two pitches and four huts is the village's capacity; the second pitch is the measure of the overflow for which the village hopes.
why.whySpot: The further pitch stands beyond the first on the same shelf, where the ground is still flat before the fall to the road.
why.whyNeighbours: It stands behind the first pitch and beside the empty ground on which the two absent tribes once camped.
why.playerPurpose: The empty pitch of Water Without Ceremony and Pitch-Rights: the ground which two tribes left on principle.
why.microGeography: The shelf falls 0.4 m from the first pitch to the second, so this pitch is the first to take run-off in the wet season.

parcels.orientationWhy: The rack turns its open face to the spur, so the rent paid by a delegation hangs in view of the next party up the track; it stands clear of the track's shoulder, on the level strip north of it.

why.what: A drying rack at the mouth of the pitch ground, hung with the fish and reed in which a delegation's rent is paid.
why.whyHere: Rent here is paid in kind as often as in coin; the rack is where the kind is seen.
why.whySpot: It stands at the mouth of the pitch ground beside the spur, between the pitch line and the gate.
why.whyNeighbours: The pitch ledger and the pitch-taker stand across the spur from it at the gate.
why.playerPurpose: A read of the village's wealth before the player has spoken to anyone in it.
why.microGeography: It stands on the 3.9 m ground where the spur begins its last climb to the gate.

routes.why: The cart line into the village. The heartland track from the Uxaneet crossing climbs the shoulder from the south-west; the same line is carried inside the boundary, up the last 120 m to the gate gap. It is not a second road beside the track. It is the track, named where the village keeps it.
The trodden ring inside the huts, from which every door in the wall is reached; it begins and ends inside the arch.
The straight walk from the arch across the clearing to the naheesh's door, the spine of the village and the line which every arrival reads first.
The path from the pier head up the bank to the arch, for guests who come by water from Uxaneet; it rises under a metre in 50 m and bends round the water-side trunk.
The short branch from the spur through the gap in the pitch line to the first shelter, worn by baggage carried in and out.

boardwalks.why: A short piled pier from the bank into the western pool, so a poled boat lands at a deck and not in the reeds.

landmarks.notes: The elder trunk: 5.8 m across and 31 m tall at scale 0.55, the beacon of both approaches.

why.what: The elder trunk of the ring, the tallest of the nine Hist columns and the one which the tree-minder watches.
why.whyHere: The village exists because nine root-joined trunks grew here in one ring; the Hist is the reason for the place, not an ornament of it.
why.whySpot: The highest trunk stands at the north of the ring on 4.0 m ground, where the knoll is broadest. It is the tallest of the nine at 31 m.
why.whyNeighbours: The naheesh's house stands at its foot inside the ring and the tree-minder's hut in the gap to its west, so the two offices of the village keep the elder trunk between them.
why.playerPurpose: The first thing seen on both approaches, above the canopy from 150 m. It is the mark by which the whole ring is found again after the canopy has hidden it.
why.microGeography: Ground at its base is 4.0 m above datum; the ring carries 1.5 m of fall from north-west to south, so the trunk stands on a shallow pad and its root flare takes the difference.

landmarks.notes: Ring trunk 2 of nine: 4.7 m across and 25 m tall at scale 0.45, 14.4 m from each neighbour along the chord.

why.whyNeighbours: It is the corner post of the two huts either side of it; the wall line of the village runs from its bark to theirs.

why.what: A root swell which lies along the ring outside the wall, joining the bases of the elder and north-eastern trunks.
why.whyHere: The joins are the ground truth of the village's dispute: one tree by the Hist's reckoning, nine by the tribes' reckoning. The joins are the thing to which both sides point.
why.whySpot: It lies on a 27.5 m radius outside the hut in the elder and north-eastern gap, clear of the wall so that a walker outside the ring sees the join and the hut behind it together.
why.whyNeighbours: Eight joins lie in eight gaps; the ninth gap, the gate, has none, which is the gap the tribes cite when they count nine trees.
why.playerPurpose: A landmark of the outer walk round the ring and a thing to be counted by a player who is asked how many trees stand here.
why.microGeography: The swell follows the ring's tangent, so it lies along the slope rather than across it and sheds the wet-season run-off round the huts.

why.whyNeighbours: Eight joins lie in eight gaps; the ninth gap, the gate, has none, which is the gap the tribes cite when they count nine trees.
why.playerPurpose: A landmark of the outer walk round the ring and a thing to be counted by a player who is asked how many trees stand here.
why.microGeography: The swell follows the ring's tangent, so it lies along the slope rather than across it and sheds the wet-season run-off round the huts.

landmarks.notes: The nest totem, north-east in the clearing between the naheesh's house and the family hut.

why.what: The totem of the uxith, the village nest, turned to face the gate across the clearing.
why.whyHere: A Hist village keeps its nest inside the enclosure of its tree; the nest is the reason the enclosure is defended.
why.whySpot: It stands on the north-eastern side of the clearing, between the naheesh's house and the first family hut, off the paths and out of the fighting ground to the east.
why.whyNeighbours: The two households charged with the eggs, the naheesh's and the eastern family's, have their doors within twelve paces of it.
why.playerPurpose: The mark by which the player reads that the ring is a nest and not a market. It is also the gated social reward of the type recipe: entry is social, not mechanical.
why.microGeography: It stands on the level northern floor of the clearing at 4.0 m, the driest ground inside the ring.

landmarks.notes: Chimes stacked eleven months of the year and hung inside the gate for the convocation month; in the convocation variant.

why.what: The frame from which the bone chimes hang inside the gate, dressed for the convocation and bare the rest of the year.
why.whyHere: Chimes at the threshold are the Hist-village custom of the region; a village that hosts delegations dresses its threshold more than most.
why.whySpot: It stands inside the gate to the right of the path to the naheesh's house, so that an arrival passes it without walking into it.
why.whyNeighbours: It sits between the gate and the pitch-taker's hut, whose household hangs and strikes the chimes.
why.playerPurpose: The first sound of the village on arrival in the convocation month. In the other eleven months it is a silent frame, which tells the player which month it is.
why.microGeography: It stands on the 4.2 m floor just inside the gate, where the ground levels after the climb from the spur.

why.what: The landing at the head of the pier in the western pool, where the boat from Uxaneet ties up.
why.whyHere: The village is reached by water from Uxaneet as often as by the road; delegations bring baggage. Baggage comes by boat.
why.whyNeighbours: The pier runs from it to the bank and the landing path climbs from the bank to the arch; the western family's hut, whose household poles the boat, stands in the wall above it.
why.playerPurpose: The arrival point for a player who comes by boat and the travel service to Uxaneet.
why.microGeography: Piles stand in the pool 2 m below the bank on its eastern shore, where the water is deep enough for a laden pole boat and the reed bed is thin.

combatSpaces.why: The eastern floor of the clearing, between the naheesh's house and the rented arc: where the felling claim of One Tree or Nine is argued and where a rite which goes wrong is fought, with the hearing of The Child of Two Hist held on the same ground.
The arch and the ground either side of it: the single gap in the stockade, where a wary village turned hostile holds its line and through which a night raid comes.
The open pitch ground between the shelters and the spur, where the baggage of Under the Overflow is opened and a rent dispute in Pitch-Rights comes to blows.

approaches.sequence: From the fork off the Archon-Gideon road the top of the elder trunk shows above the mangrove canopy, 31 m against 10 m at 116 m off; the track drops into low ground and the canopy closes over it for 60 m; at the pitch ground the whole ring rises as one grey wall of trunks and hut roofs; then the arch reads as the single gap in it, with the chime frame inside; through the arch the path runs straight to the round house.
approaches.wayfinding: Keep the tallest trunk ahead; the arch is the single gap in the wall. The path through it runs to the round house.
approaches.notes: The catalogue's road discovery. The spur bends twice, at the pitch ground and at the foot of the knoll, so the gate is not seen from the road; the elder trunk is.

approaches.fromDirection: west, up the pool from the Uxaneet channel
approaches.sequence: From the water the nine trunks stand above the reeds like the teeth of a comb, the elder trunk tallest among them; as the boat noses to the pier the bank's mangroves take them one by one; from the pier head the western huts and the wall read together above the bank; the landing path climbs and bends round the water-side trunk, then the arch opens on the left hand.
approaches.wayfinding: From the pier, climb towards the gap in the trunks; the arch is round the trunk on the right.
approaches.notes: The travel service from Uxaneet lands here. The bank stands 2 m above the water at the pier head and the path rises under a metre in 50 m; the arch is hidden from the pier by the bank's mangroves and re-found at the bend.

travelServices.timetable: on request; hourly during the convocation

assetConstraints: district.nine-trunks.ring is one kit set (settlement-mud-v1). Every piece inside the ring comes from it: huts, round house, arch, deck, totem, chime frame, woven panels. No root-kit walkway or house form stands inside the ring.

the nine trunk columns and eight root joins are landmarks from the tropical set (anvilgianttrunk, anvil_root01, one author, composited together in flora-province-v1) at a uniform scale of 0.45 (0.55 for the elder trunk); no piece is attached to them, so no piece is asked to span between two trunks

the delegation canvas on the pitch ground is the mud kit's open shelter (argoniantent02), which has no interior and so no door; the closed tent (argoniantent01) is not used because it would need an interior claim a canvas cannot honour
the naheesh's round house (bmv hutexterior) is a shell in its kit; its interior is claimed from dungeon-root-v1 pending an owner decision on the medium Argonian hall interior

provision.notes: LH51 takes the pitch ground, the ledger station at the gate and the pitch-taker's hut; LH52 takes the eastern root join and the felling scene on the eastern floor of the clearing; LH53 takes the baggage under the first shelter and the pitch-taker's household; LH37 takes the two empty rented huts and the empty pitch; MQ19 takes the naheesh's house, the tree-minder's hut and the minder's deck.

networkTerminals.why: The heartland track reaches the village on the one shoulder that carries a cart above the pool's flood line; it crosses the boundary here and the spur carries it the last 120 m to the gate gap, so track and street are one line.
